data.name: Astrohazard Solutions Ltd.
data.detailed_description:
Astrohazard Solutions Ltd. is an interstellar and interspecies corporation dealing mainly with removing and redirecting asteroids and other cosmic junk that threatens their Clients.

In this story-driven, action 2D Sci-Fi game, the player assumes the role of a fresh employee (Operator) hired by Astrohazard Solutions. Operator is assigned various space contracts for different Clients, each with their own specific (and sometimes weird) policies and requests. Operator's main tool is the AstroBeam™ cannon, mounted on a drone, a spaceship, or a turret. Payments for successfully completed assignments can be used between contracts to buy upgrades and improve technology in Astrohazard Solutions’ HQ. In the Headquarters, Operator can also interact with four other employees: Directron (boss), Stasis (intern), Vorp (Chief Engineer) and Gor (Alien Resources manager), and experience some other aspects of corporate daily routine...



Main features:
  • Innovative AstroBeam™ physics: gradually slow down and push away incoming hazards instead of destroying them
  • Diversified mission goals with three distinctive game modes
  • Detailed storyline, full of ironic humor and references to modern corporate culture, as well as to well-known sci-fi motifs
  • Memorable characters with unique personalities
  • Distinctive, cartoon art style

reviews.review:
Astrohazard Solutions Ltd. is a small 2D space game with a really fun idea behind it. Instead of blowing up asteroids and other space junk, I am hired as a new employee of a strange interstellar company and my job is to redirect those hazards away from the company's clients. The main tool I get is the AstroBeam, which lets me slow things down and push objects away rather than simply destroying everything. I like that because it gives the game its own identity straight away. It feels like a simple arcade idea, but there is a bit more thought involved than I expected.

The AstroBeam is easily the best part for me. I have to control the incoming objects and guide them away from whatever I am supposed to protect, which means I am constantly thinking about their speed and direction. It is satisfying when I manage to push something away at the last second and save the target. There are three different mission types as well, so the objective is not always exactly the same. The game does a good job of keeping the basic mechanic simple while still giving me something to concentrate on.

I also like the corporate setting because it gives the game a lot more personality than it would have had as a straightforward asteroid game. I am working for Astrohazard Solutions and can return to the company's headquarters between contracts. There I can talk to Directron, Stasis, Vorp and Gor, with each character having their own personality and role in the strange company. I can also spend the money I earn from successful contracts on upgrades and improvements. The humour is built around corporate culture and science fiction, and I think that combination works surprisingly well.

The main weakness for me is that the actual gameplay is fairly limited. Once I understand how the AstroBeam works, most of the challenge comes from getting better at using the same basic mechanic in different situations. That can still be fun, but I do not think there is enough here to keep me interested for a huge amount of time. The game is designed as a short experience, and the average session is only a few hours, so I think it works better as something I finish over a couple of sittings rather than a game I expect to keep playing for weeks.

I also think the presentation is charming without being particularly impressive. The cartoon art style suits the strange characters and silly corporate setting, and I like how the headquarters gives me somewhere to go between missions. There are also sixteen achievements and Steam leaderboards, which give me a few extra reasons to replay the missions and improve my results. At the same time, the visuals and environments are fairly simple, so most of the appeal still comes from the gameplay idea and the writing rather than the production values.

What I appreciate most is that Astrohazard Solutions Ltd. does not try to turn its simple idea into something unnecessarily complicated. I can understand the basic objective quickly, but there is still enough physics involved in controlling the AstroBeam that I have to pay attention. The different contracts and upgrades give the campaign some structure, while the characters and humour make the whole thing feel more memorable. It is also a free game, which makes the short length much easier for me to accept. I would rather have a focused little game like this than one that adds filler just to make the campaign longer.

Overall, Astrohazard Solutions Ltd. is a creative little space game that I think deserves credit for doing something different with a very familiar setting. I like the AstroBeam mechanic, the unusual corporate story, the characters, the different mission types and the simple cartoon presentation. The limited length and relatively narrow gameplay loop stop it from reaching my higher ratings, but I think the game knows exactly what it wants to be and does it well. For me, it is a good short experience that is easy to understand, has plenty of personality and manages to make pushing space junk around feel much more entertaining than it sounds.

Rating: 7/10
